name: Ramviyas Nattanmai Parasuraman
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
department: School of Computing; Heterogeneous Robotics (HeRo) Lab
fitReason: Strong CS and embodied-AI overlap in semantic perception, uncertainty-aware mapping, low-supervision LLM adaptation and robot information gathering. A software-first mapping/evaluation contribution could be scoped for a short project if the host agrees; the lab also explicitly studies human-robot teams and teleoperation.

physicalEvidence.summary: The 2026 primary paper SK: Semantic Kernel for Robotic Information Gathering identifies the authors with UGA and reports a Rover-MAX mobile robot autonomously exploring a 10-by-13-metre multi-room laboratory. It collects Wi-Fi signal and RGB-D observations; SLAM/object detection yields a scene graph, and LLM-derived Gaussian-process kernels model the signal field. Six real trials are reported. This is actual local robot sensing/modeling evidence, not merely simulated navigation or a model directly commanding robot joints.

shortVisit.summary: The current official department and lab contact pages establish a research contact but no explicit external visitor/intern opening. An older personal homepage invites graduate/undergraduate research interest but is last updated July 2020; its Assistant Professor title is obsolete and its recruitment paragraph is not treated as a current summer route. No 2027 dates, eight-week duration, funding or external master's hosting commitment was found.

unknowns: Current official directory says Associate Professor; use it rather than the outdated personal homepage's Assistant Professor title.
The lab website has 2026 publications/news despite an old October 2021 footer. Freshness rests on the dated 2026 paper and official news, not the footer.
Research fit does not establish eight-week project feasibility, supervision, international appointment eligibility, funding or permission to be wholly self-funded.
The spatial-model paper combines scene reasoning with probabilistic sensing. It is not evidence of a general-purpose autonomous manipulation policy or unrestricted human-facing deployment.
Other 2026 collaborative HARMONIC work includes a physical tabletop manipulator, but that collaboration was not used to claim ownership of another institution's hardware.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
